action: If you run Metabase, apply the latest vendor patch and review access logs from August 2026 onward. Patients notified by Dorsata's provider partners should monitor insurance statements and accounts.
exec: A zero-day in a widely used analytics tool exposed patient data at a healthcare vendor; other Metabase users may face the same risk.
plain: Hackers used an unknown flaw in a data-reporting tool to reach health records of about 58,000 patients held by a US health-tech company.

sources.name: Dorsata notice filed with the California Attorney General

summary: The women's-health technology company reported that an unauthorized party exploited a previously unknown flaw in its Metabase business intelligence software between August 10 and 12 and reached a database holding information on 58,249 patients of provider partners. Exposed data includes names, birth dates, treatment details, medications and insurance information; Dorsata's notice says Social Security numbers were not involved. A researcher says the Dire Wolf group later used the same flaw. No CVE was given.
title: Metabase zero-day exploited in Dorsata breach affecting 58,249 patients

validation.note: Two publishers state the breach: the Dorsata notice filed with the California Attorney General and HIPAA Journal. Primary: Dorsata's own notice letter on the California Attorney General's site (read 22 Nov) states Metabase's 12 August notice, the 10-12 August access window and that Social Security numbers were not involved; it gives no count and does not call the flaw a zero-day. The 58,249 count, data types and Dire Wolf link rest on HIPAA Journal. The notice's return address is Charlottesville, VA; HIPAA Journal gives Arlington, VA.

review.note: Compared with HIPAA Journal (13 Nov): Aug 10-12 window, data types, Dire Wolf via VenariX correct; added the 58,249 figure to the summary
